data.content_ref: inline:The defense collapses because Popper's own concept of 'verisimilitude' was proven by Tichý and Miller (1974) to be logically incoherent within a deterministic framework: without probabilistic measures, one cannot formally compare the 'truth-content' vs 'falsity-content' of two false theories to establish that one is 'closer' to the truth. By grounding the pragmatic wager in verisimilitude while explicitly rejecting probability, the target relies on a broken metric. If verisimilitude cannot be defined or compared without smuggling in probabilistic assumptions (which Popper rejected), then the 'non-inductive selection rule' described has no operative mechanism, rendering the preference indefensible on Popper's own strict terms.
